processErrors.lesson: Budget should be treated as maximum exposure, never a required amount to deploy.
processErrors.note: The final four additional wagers (Texas TT Over 4.5, Kyle Harrison 6+ Ks, Yordan Alvarez 2+ hits, Blake Snell Under 15 outs) lost $48.08 combined and converted a previously positive card into a losing slate.

processErrors.lesson: The highest-ranked standalone opportunities appeared materially stronger than the lower-ranked bets added to fill the available budget. Stop wagering when the edge disappears.
processErrors.note: Card quality deteriorated as additional capital was forced into weaker late-card positions.

proposedInvestigations.lesson: Continue evaluating the complete archived Kalshi market universe rather than limiting analysis to sides/F5.
Every recommended market should have an independent fair-probability estimate or defensible probability range.
Do not automatically translate a starting-pitcher mismatch into an F5 winner wager.
Explicitly model F5 tie probability.
Apply a correlation penalty when multiple positions depend on the same pitcher/game thesis.
Returning-from-IL starters should receive automatic uncertainty and stake downgrades, particularly for pitcher overs.
Team totals need independent team run projections rather than simply fading a weak opposing starter.
Hitter multi-hit props require a real plate-appearance/hit-distribution projection before recommendation.
Soft managerial workload expectations should not be treated as hard pitch/innings limits for pitcher-outs markets.
Do not interpret one slate as enough evidence to abandon F5 markets or declare pitcher-K props categorically superior; track performance by market family over a meaningful sample.
